results.summary: The pattern recurs, and the worst instance is not SwiftUI-vs-UIKit but UIKit-vs-UIKit. The Atlas tab's hero is a 280-420pt SCNView with `allowsCameraControl = true` sitting directly inside the tab's vertical ScrollView; SceneKit's camera pan and UIScrollView's pan both claim the vertical drag with no failure relationship between them, so the Atlas tab is likely unscrollable anywhere over its own hero, and the overlay hint advertises the conflicting gesture ("Drag to rotate"). Second, every message action in Chat (Copy, Regenerate, Share, Details, Report, Export Trace, Go Deeper, Translate, Illustrate, Thumbs) hangs off exactly one `.onTapGesture` layered over `.textSelection(.enabled)` markdown, with no second route to any of them. Third, the fixed ContainerPicker bug has a verbatim twin: SourceChip carries `.onLongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0, pressing:)` on a Button inside a horizontal ScrollView, on a ~21pt tap target. Two smaller affordance gaps round it out (List rows and Settings mode rows driven by `.onTapGesture` instead of Button, so they never flash on press and carry no `.isButton` trait). I also checked and cleared a lot: ContainerPill is genuinely fixed, DocumentLibraryView's NavigationLink+contextMenu is textbook, the UnifiedMetricsBar drag handle is a sibling of its ScrollView and pinned outside the transcript so it has no ancestor pan to fight, the onboarding paged TabView's inner ScrollViews are orthogonal-axis, the MotherboardHUD pan lives on its own UIWindow by design, `hapticTap`'s `simultaneousGesture` has zero call sites, ThreadSidebarView's scrim is an HStack sibling and does not overlay the list, and the app contains exactly one DragGesture and it is vertical, so nothing competes with the NavigationStack swipe-back edge. Everything here needs a device to confirm the arbitration outcome; the structural conflicts are certain from source, the felt symptoms are inferred.

issues.what: The Atlas tab's hero 3D scene is an SCNView with `allowsCameraControl = true` mounted directly inside the tab's root vertical ScrollView. SceneKit installs its own UIPanGestureRecognizer (plus pinch and rotate) on the SCNView; the enclosing ScrollView's pan is on an ancestor. Neither declares a failure requirement against the other, and SceneKit's camera pan begins on near-zero movement while UIScrollView's pan must first exceed its slop. Chain: ContentView.swift:275-283 (Atlas tab) -> AdaptiveVisualizationsView.swift:104 `ScrollView {` -> :117 `hero3DAtlasSection(profile:)` -> :229 `CompactAtlasSceneView(height: atlasMode == .expanded ? 420 : 280)` -> :2947 `Embedding3DSceneView` -> Embedding3DView.swift:3377 `SceneViewContainer` -> :3402 `SCNView` -> :3423 `view.allowsCameraControl = true`.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You open Atlas, try to scroll down to the insights and stats, and the page does not move. The globe spins instead. The hero is 280pt tall compact and 420pt expanded with only 8pt of scrollable gutter either side (AdaptiveVisualizationsView.swift:238), so the only reliable way down the page is to find the thin header, legend or stats strips. Pull-to-refresh is on the same ScrollView (:211) and is equally unreachable from the hero. The scene even prints "Drag to rotate • Pinch to zoom" over itself (:3019), so the app is advertising the gesture that eats the scroll. This is the single worst felt-navigation defect I found: one of five tabs reads as frozen.
issues.fix: Gate the inline scene's camera control behind an explicit engagement instead of having it always on. In `SceneViewContainer`, drive `allowsCameraControl` from a new `isInteractive` parameter that `CompactAtlasSceneView` sets false until the user taps the scene once (the tap recognizer at Embedding3DView.swift:3408 already exists and can carry the engage action), and clear it when the scene scrolls out of view or the user taps elsewhere. While disengaged the scene still renders, still auto-rotates, and still responds to the point-tap hit test; while engaged every orbit, pinch and rotate gesture behaves exactly as it does today. Show the existing hint text as an "Tap to explore" affordance in the disengaged state. Alternative if you would rather not add the tap: give SceneKit's pan recognizer a delegate whose `gestureRecognizerShouldBegin` returns false for a predominantly vertical initial translation while the enclosing scroll view can still scroll that way. That keeps orbit instant but gives up pure-vertical orbit mid-page, and it depends on reassigning a delegate SceneKit owns, so I would treat it as the riskier option. Either way the fullscreen atlas (AdaptiveVisualizationsView.swift:314-322, presented at :151) is untouched and remains the unconstrained full-gesture surface.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Nothing is removed. Orbit, pinch, rotate, the point-tap hit test (Embedding3DView.swift:3439-3459), autorotate, depth cue, labels, projection switching and the fullscreen route all remain. The engagement gate adds a step in front of orbit; it does not delete orbit. Against that it restores scrolling and pull-to-refresh over the hero, which are currently unavailable there at all. I know nothing is lost because `allowsCameraControl` is the only thing being conditioned: `configure(_:)` at :3420-3425 sets scene, lighting and background independently of it, and the explicit tap recognizer at :3408 is added in `makeUIView` and is unaffected.

issues.what: The message action bar has exactly one entry point, and that entry point is a SwiftUI `TapGesture` layered over text that has UIKit text-interaction recognizers attached. MessageBubbleV2.swift:175-181 puts `.onTapGesture { showActions.toggle() }` on the whole bubble. The bubble's content is `MarkdownText` (:96-100), whose single-paragraph fast path is `InlineMarkdownText` (MarkdownRenderer.swift:707), which applies `.textSelection(.enabled)` on both branches (MarkdownRenderer.swift:466 and :471); the block path's `CodeBlockView` does the same at :737. Grep confirms `showActions` is set true in exactly one place, MessageBubbleV2.swift:177 — lines 361 and 407 only set it false.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You tap a reply to copy it and sometimes the toolbar appears and sometimes the text selection loupe does, or nothing does. Because there is no second route, an arbitration loss is not a cosmetic annoyance: Copy, Regenerate, Show Details, Share, Hide, Report, Export Pipeline Trace, Go Deeper, Translate, Illustrate and both feedback buttons (MessageBubbleV2.swift:187-206) all become momentarily unreachable, and the user's only recourse is to tap again. Retrying a tap is the exact sensation of a slow app even when nothing is slow.
issues.fix: Add a `.contextMenu` to the bubble carrying the same action set the bar exposes, alongside the existing tap. UIKit arbitrates `.contextMenu` against text interaction and against the transcript's scroll pan itself, so it always resolves, which is precisely why the ContainerPicker fix worked (see the rationale already written at ContainerPicker.swift:216-233). Also add `.accessibilityAction`s for the same set so VoiceOver has a route that does not depend on the visual toolbar at all. Leave the tap exactly as it is.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Strictly additive. The tap-to-reveal bar stays, `.textSelection(.enabled)` stays so copy-by-selection still works, and every action keeps its existing closure — the context menu calls the same handlers `MessageActionsBar` is wired to at MessageBubbleV2.swift:187-206. I know nothing is lost because no existing modifier is removed or reordered; a second, independently-arbitrated path is added to actions that currently have one path.

issues.what: The same construct that was just fixed in ContainerPicker, unchanged. `SourceChip` is a `Button` with `.buttonStyle(.plain)` (SourceChipsView.swift:94, :125) carrying a hand-rolled `.onLongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0, pressing:)` at :126 purely to drive a `scaleEffect` press state (:119), and it lives inside `ScrollView(.horizontal, showsIndicators: false)` at :182. The press state duplicates what `ButtonStyle`'s `configuration.isPressed` gives with correct arbitration — the project already has exactly that in `HapticButtonStyle` at Theme.swift:851-874. Separately the tap target is roughly 21pt tall: 9pt text (:105, :110) plus `.padding(.vertical, 5)` (:117).
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Two symptoms stack. The chip is a ~21pt-tall target in a strip you are also trying to swipe, so misses are common and a miss is indistinguishable from a lag. And when the press does register, the shrink animation is driven by a gesture that is competing with the scroll pan rather than by the button's own press state, so the chip can stick shrunk after a scroll steals the touch, or flash without the tap landing. A control that visibly reacts and then does nothing is worse than one that does nothing quietly.
issues.fix: Delete the `.onLongPressGesture` at :126 and move the `scaleEffect(isPressed ? 0.95 : 1.0)` into a small `ButtonStyle` reading `configuration.isPressed`, applied via `.buttonStyle(...)` in place of `.plain`. Then give the chip a real target: raise `.padding(.vertical, 5)` (:117) or add `.contentShape(Capsule())` over a `.frame(minHeight: 44)` so the touch region reaches 44pt without the capsule growing visually. While in there, ChatScreen.swift:791 constructs `SourceChipsView(chunks: currentRetrievedChunks) {}` with an empty `onTap`, so on that fallback sheet path the chips animate their press and fire `DSHaptics.light()` (:93) and then do nothing — worth either wiring or making non-interactive.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Identical rendering and identical behaviour. The 0.95 scale, its 0.1s easeInOut, the light haptic, the `onTap` callback and the accessibility label at :131 all survive; only the mechanism driving `isPressed` changes, from a competing gesture to the Button's own press state. The tap region grows, which can only add reachable area. I know nothing is lost because `.onLongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0, ..., perform: {})` has an empty `perform` — its sole output is the `pressing:` boolean, which `configuration.isPressed` reproduces exactly.

issues.what: The Intelligence Mode selector, the primary control in Settings, is driven by `.onTapGesture` on a composed card rather than a Button. SettingsView.swift:2157-2175 attaches the gesture to `intelligenceModeRow(mode:isSelected:)` (:2334-2388). Related: `canSelectMode` at :2431-2437 looks like a predicate but mutates `planEntryPoint` and `showPlanSheet`, and the `DSHaptics.selection()` at :2166 sits after the guard, so the blocked path fires no haptic.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You press Deep Think and the card does not acknowledge the touch at all; the only feedback is the state flip after the fact, behind a 0.3s spring. On a locked Maximum row you get no haptic either, and the plan sheet takes a moment to animate in, so the interval between finger-down and any response reads as the app thinking. VoiceOver gets no button trait and no selected trait, so the whole picker announces as a text group.
issues.fix: Wrap the row in `Button { ... } label: { intelligenceModeRow(mode: mode, isSelected: ...) }` with `.buttonStyle(.plain)` plus a style supplying a press response, and add `.accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? [.isButton, .isSelected] : .isButton)`. Move `DSHaptics.selection()` (or a distinct blocked-path haptic) ahead of the `canSelectMode` guard so a blocked press still confirms it registered, and split `canSelectMode` into a pure predicate plus an explicit `presentPlanSheet()` call so the side effect is visible at the call site.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Every path is kept: mode switching, the spring animation, the selection haptic, the Deep Think metrics reset at :2172, and the paywall presentation for locked Maximum. The paywall behaviour in particular is unchanged — splitting `canSelectMode` moves where `showPlanSheet = true` is written, not whether it is written. The blocked path gains a haptic it currently lacks; it loses nothing. I know nothing is lost because the Button's action body is the existing closure verbatim.

issues.what: Chunk Inspector list rows are tapped through `.onTapGesture` inside a `List` rather than a Button. ChunkInspectorView.swift:254-256: `ChunkRowView(chunk: chunk).contentShape(Rectangle()).onTapGesture { selectedChunk = chunk }`. The `contentShape` is correct so the hit area is right; what is missing is the row press treatment and the button semantics a `List` gives a Button for free.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Rows do not flash when pressed, so on a list where opening a chunk does real retrieval work there is a dead interval with zero confirmation that the tap landed. It is the cheapest possible version of feeling slow: the work may be instant and it still reads as a dropped tap. VoiceOver also gets no `.isButton` trait, so the rows do not announce as activatable.
issues.fix: `Button { selectedChunk = chunk } label: { ChunkRowView(chunk: chunk) }` with `.buttonStyle(.plain)`, keeping `.contentShape(Rectangle())`. In a `List` that restores the standard row highlight and the button trait with no styling change.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Same target action, same hit region, same row rendering. The only difference is that the row now flashes on press and announces as a button. I know nothing is lost because the closure is unchanged and `.contentShape(Rectangle())` is retained, so the tappable area does not shrink.

results.summary: Real findings, and the pattern is consistent: the motion is *written* but not *wired*. Four separate transitions (message insertion, metrics bar, follow-up chips, writing-tools overlay) are declared in source and never run, because the state that drives them is mutated outside any animation transaction, or because `.animation(_:value:)` sits inside the `if` it is supposed to animate. MessageBubbleV2.swift:175-179 does it correctly, which is how you can tell the others are oversights rather than choices. The net effect is that the app's highest-intent moment — pressing Send — produces zero connecting motion: the bubble pops in, then an unrelated spring scrolls the list, and a metrics bar materialises above and shoves the conversation down in a hard jump. Second cluster: the streaming path animates what it says it does not (`scrollToBottom(animated: false)` runs `withAnimation`, MessageListV2.swift:167) on an arbitrary modulo throttle whose cadence depends on adaptive chunk size, producing jerky follow and yanking the user back when they read a few lines up. Third: the Silicon HUD defaults ON (SettingsStore.swift:581), is mounted on four of five tabs, and its blurred glow gets a fresh implicit animation 25 times a second from a MainActor pulse loop, over the list you are scrolling, during generation. Honest negative on one thing I was asked to check: `glassEffect` is NOT the scroll cost. It appears on chips, three buttons and two containers (Theme.swift:321-368 and five call sites) and on no list row; bubble shadows are opacity 0.04 / radius 2. The offscreen work worth measuring is the HUD's `.blur(radius:)` at MotherboardHUDView.swift:577 and 640, not the glass. Also: 14 `repeatForever` animations and exactly one reader of `accessibilityReduceMotion` (OnboardingChecklistView.swift:36) — Reduce Motion is honoured in onboarding and nowhere else. No hard-boundary file is involved in any fix; ChatScreen mutates `[ChatMessage]` but ChatMessage.swift itself needs no change.

issues.what: The message-insertion transition is declared but never runs: no site that mutates `messages` wraps the change in an animation transaction, so SwiftUI has no transaction to drive the insertion/removal.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You press Send and the bubble is just suddenly there — no motion links your tap to the thing that appeared. A beat later the list springs to the bottom in a separate, unrelated animation, so the arrival reads as two disconnected events instead of one gesture landing.
issues.fix: Wrap the mutation sites in the same curve the scroll already uses: `withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.8))` around `messages.append(userMessage)` (ChatScreen.swift:2516), `messages.append(message)` in appendAndPersistMessage (ChatScreen.swift:1729), and the two `messages.removeAll()` calls (ChatScreen.swift:1751, 1796). That puts the insertion and the existing `scrollToBottom(animated: true)` spring (MessageListV2.swift:162) in one transaction, so the bubble rises into place as the list follows it. Leave the `.transition` at MessageListV2.swift:92-95 exactly as written.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Nothing is removed or gated. The asymmetric transition already exists in source at lines 92-95 and is currently dead; this only supplies the transaction it needs. Message content, ordering, `persistChatHistory` and the container-override path are untouched — the change is purely the transaction wrapper around an assignment that already happens.

issues.what: `scrollToBottom(animated: false)` is animated — it runs `withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.12))` — and it is driven by a modulo predicate whose firing rate depends on the adaptive streaming chunk size, not on time.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: The transcript tracks the stream unevenly: glued for a stretch, then drifting, then snapping. And an animated programmatic scroll competes with your finger, so trying to re-read a few lines while an answer streams pulls you back down — you have to scroll more than the 80pt un-pin threshold (line 153-154) before the app will leave you alone.
issues.fix: In the `animated: false` branch (lines 166-169) call `proxy.scrollTo("bottom", anchor: .bottom)` with no `withAnimation`, so the follow is a plain offset set that a touch can override. Replace the `newText.count % 80 < 20` predicate at line 140 with a time-based throttle (store a `lastAutoScroll: Date` and scroll at most every ~100ms), so cadence no longer swings with the 50/80/120-char adaptive chunk sizes chosen at ChatScreen.swift:3053-3071.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Auto-follow during streaming stays, the pin/un-pin detection via BottomAnchorYPreferenceKey stays, the 80pt threshold stays, and the `animated: true` spring path for new messages and thinking events (lines 134, 148) is untouched. Only the streaming branch stops animating and starts throttling on a clock instead of on character count.

issues.what: `withAnimation(.linear(duration: 0.04))` wraps a plain string append in the streaming pump, opening an animation transaction over the whole transcript subtree 12-25 times a second for a mutation that cannot interpolate.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Arriving text looks soft and smeary rather than crisp, and these transactions overlap the animated scroll from the same state change, so two competing animations run on the same view every pump tick — at the exact moment the device is busiest generating.
issues.fix: Append plainly: `streamingText.append(nextChunk)` with no `withAnimation`. If the soft reveal was intentional, express it locally instead — `.contentTransition(.opacity)` on the streaming `MarkdownText` (MessageListV2.swift:232-236) animates the glyph swap without opening a transaction that reaches the rest of the list.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Identical characters at an identical cadence. The adaptive backlog logic (chunk size 50/80/120, cadence 40/60/80ms, lines 3057-3071), the `updateSpeedHistory()` sparkline call at line 3083, and the finish-fast path all stay exactly as they are. Only the scope of the animation transaction changes.

issues.what: Three transitions are placed inside the `if` branch they are meant to animate, with `.animation(_:value:)` also inside the branch, so the modifier is torn down along with the content and neither insertion nor removal animates. None of the driving state is mutated inside `withAnimation`.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: The instant you send, a metrics bar materialises above the transcript and shoves the entire conversation down in one frame, while the follow-up chip row vanishes in the same frame. Two hard layout jumps stacked on the app's most-repeated action. It reads as the screen glitching rather than responding.
issues.fix: Hang the animation off a parent that survives the swap: put `.animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.2), value: consolidatedMetricsData != nil)`, `.animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.25), value: followUpSuggestions.isEmpty)` and `.animation(.spring(response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.8), value: writingToolsProcessing)` on the `mainContentArea` VStack (line 2012) and delete the in-branch copies at 2027, 2141 and 2166. Alternatively wrap the mutations (2116, 2250, 2280, 2285, 2484, 2831, 636, 1766, 1809, 1880) in `withAnimation`. MessageBubbleV2.swift:175-179 with its transition at line 209 is the working template already in this codebase.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Every bar appears and disappears at exactly the same times, on the same conditions, with the same content. The `.transition` declarations stay where they are. Nothing is hidden, delayed past its trigger, or removed — the only change is that three already-written transitions start running.

issues.what: `chatContentArea` hard-swaps between the first-query hero and the transcript with no transition, and the swap destroys and rebuilds `MessageListV2`, discarding its scroll position and pinned-to-bottom state.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Your first message replaces the whole suggestion screen with a hard cut — the most consequential moment in the app has the least motion. New Chat and Clear Chat (lines 1751, 1796) cut back just as abruptly. Because the gate is `messages.isEmpty` (line 1562), the list view identity dies on every flip, so `isPinnedToBottom` (MessageListV2.swift:173) resets too.
issues.fix: Give both branches a matched `.transition(.opacity)` and drive the flip from an animation on the enclosing VStack keyed on `shouldShowFirstQueryHero` (paired with the fix above, one `.animation` on `mainContentArea` covers it). Separately, note that `EmptyStateV2` at MessageListV2.swift:76-78 is unreachable while this gate exists — worth confirming with the owner which empty state is meant to win before touching it.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Both screens keep every control: starter prompts, categories, the refresh button, the transcript, and all message callbacks. The gate condition is unchanged, so the same screen shows at the same times — it crossfades instead of cutting.

issues.what: Source chips replay a 350ms staggered reveal every time they scroll back into view, and each chip carries a manual `onLongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0, pressing:)` over a Button inside a horizontal ScrollView — the same arbitration pattern already replaced with `.contextMenu` on library chips.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Scrolling back up through the transcript makes old answers' source chips flutter in again, one by one, as if they were new — motion that says 'something just happened' when nothing did. And a chip can stick in its pressed state or swallow a horizontal scroll, because the press gesture and the scroll pan are fighting for the same touch.
issues.fix: Replace lines 126-129 with a `ButtonStyle` that reads `configuration.isPressed` for the 0.95 scale — SwiftUI cancels that state automatically when a scroll begins, which a manual long-press does not. For the replay: `appearedCount` is `@State` in a view living inside LazyVStack rows (used at RetrievalSourcesTray.swift:112 and ChatScreen.swift:791), so it is destroyed on recycle; either drop the per-index `.delay(Double(index) * 0.05)` at line 39 so the row is simply present, or key the reveal off the chunk data rather than `.onAppear` (lines 56-62).
issues.functionalityPreserved: All six chips, the +N MoreChip, the tap-to-open-details action, the press-scale feedback, and both accessibility labels (lines 63 and 130) stay. The press affordance is not removed — it moves to the mechanism that cancels correctly. ContainerPicker.swift:216-219 documents the identical migration already made for library chips.

issues.what: A 25Hz MainActor loop writes `intensity` in discrete steps, and each write restarts a 20-30ms implicit animation on a blurred, screen-sized glow that is mounted on four of five tabs by default.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: There is a blurred glow re-animating 25-33 times a second on top of the list you are trying to scroll, and it runs hardest during generation — precisely when the main thread has least headroom. Separately, a user who turns on Reduce Motion still gets shimmer bars, a blinking cursor, spinning icons and pulsing pills, because 14 `repeatForever` sites exist and only OnboardingChecklistView.swift:36 reads the setting.
issues.fix: Drive the sine oscillation from a single `repeatForever` animation (or a TimelineView) on one value, instead of 25 discrete state writes per second that each restart the `.animation(.linear(duration: 0.03), value: intensity)` at MotherboardHUDView.swift:615 (also 663, 702) over the `.blur(radius:)` at 577 and 640. Separately, read `@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion)` at the `repeatForever` sites — MessageListV2.swift:254 and 370, RetrievalSourcesTray.swift:189, StatusPillV2.swift:106, UnifiedMetricsBar.swift:520, 1174, 1262, ThinkingStreamView.swift:355, ModelStatusIndicator.swift:124, LiveTelemetryStatsView.swift:115, Theme.swift:223 — and substitute a static value when it is on.
issues.functionalityPreserved: The HUD stays on by default (SettingsStore.swift:581 unchanged), same glow, same colours, same component intensities, same legend, same user-controlled `hudGlowIntensity`. The oscillation looks the same; it is produced by one animation instead of 25 restarts per second. Honouring Reduce Motion adds respect for a setting the user chose — it removes no animation from anyone who has not asked for that.

issues.what: The suggestion-refresh icon rewinds when it finishes: `rotationEffect(.degrees(isRefreshing ? 360 : 0))` targets 0° on completion and the `.default` branch eases it backwards from wherever the loop stopped.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Every refresh ends with the spinner visibly un-spinning. A reverse rotation is the universal sign for undo, so the completion reads as a cancellation.
issues.fix: Accumulate the angle instead of toggling between two: keep `@State private var refreshRotation: Double = 0`, add 360 per cycle while running, and stop adding when done so the icon just holds. `.symbolEffect(.rotate, isActive: isRefreshing)` is the cleaner iOS 26 route. The same shape exists at CoreValidationView.swift:63 (DEBUG diagnostics), worth fixing in the same pass.
issues.functionalityPreserved: The spinner, the `.disabled(isRefreshing)` guard at line 3826, and the 'Refresh suggestions' accessibility label at line 3827 all stay. The rotation still runs for exactly as long as the refresh does — it just stops instead of reversing.

results.summary:
The five tabs are one `TabView(selection:)` with five `NavigationStack` roots, tagged `.chat/.documents/.visualizations/.database/.settings` (/Users/gunnarhostetler/Documents/GitHub/OpenIntelligence/OpenIntelligence/App/ContentView.swift:254-304). Three things in this dimension are clean and I want to say so rather than pad: (a) no `.id()` is applied to any container anywhere in the app — the only `.id()` calls are per-row identity inside scroll content (MessageListV2.swift:77-119, ThinkingStreamView.swift:152, IngestionQueueOverlay.swift:75), so nothing forces a tab teardown; (b) no view model is built in a `View.init` — every long-lived object is a `@StateObject` on ContentView (ContentView.swift:14-21) or a shared singleton, and the five tab roots have trivial or absent inits (ChatScreen.swift:194, DocumentLibraryView.swift:84), so declaring all five in one ViewBuilder costs nothing; (c) `@State` genuinely survives tab switches, so selections, sheet flags and expanded sections come back intact.

The defects are all one shape, and it is the opposite of the one I expected: state survives, but appearance callbacks throw it away. Every tab root restarts its `.task`/`onAppear` when the user returns, and four of the five then either recompute from zero while showing a spinner over data that is still in memory, or actively destroy user work. The worst is Chat: returning to the tab mid-answer runs the container-change task from the top, which cancels the streaming query and discards the partial text — the "Stop" button preserves the partial answer, this path does not. Second worst is that the transcript force-scrolls to the bottom on every return, so you cannot leave the tab while reading an older answer. Atlas, its 3D scene, and the Database overview each replace populated content with a loading state on return; the visualization engine even maintains a `profileCache` that is written and never read (LibraryVisualizationEngine.swift:304, 381).

Separately, navigation is not addressable: no `NavigationStack` in the app takes a `path` binding (only the Glossary does, GlossaryViews.swift:179), so deep links and Spotlight can select a tab but cannot reach its root, re-tapping the active tab does nothing, and there is no `@SceneStorage` anywhere — tab selection and the composer draft do not survive a relaunch.

Everything below is read off source. The premise that SwiftUI restarts `.task` and fires `onAppear`/`onDisappear` on a `TabView` tab change needs a device confirmation, though the repo already contains strong circumstantial evidence for it: ChatScreen keeps an `isAppeared` flag set in `onAppear`/`onDisappear` (ChatScreen.swift:885, 888) specifically to defer suggested-question refreshes while the Chat tab is not showing, which only makes sense if the author observed those callbacks firing on tab switches.

One out-of-dimension note in passing, since the brief asked to treat the chip/scroll-gesture conflict as a pattern: SourceChipsView.swift:126 attaches `.onLongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0, pressing:)` to a `Button` that already has `.buttonStyle(.plain)`, inside a horizontal `ScrollView` (line 34). It is the same recognizer-versus-pan shape as the library chips, and the press state it drives is already available from the button style. Whoever owns the gesture dimension should look at it.

issues.what: Returning to the Chat tab while an answer is streaming cancels the query and discards the partial text. The `.task(id: activeContainerId)` body runs on every appearance, not only when the container id changes, and its first four statements cancel the in-flight query unconditionally — before the `isSameChatContainer` guard that scopes the rest of the body.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You ask a question, glance at Documents to check a filename, come back, and the answer is gone with no explanation — no partial text, no error, just an idle composer. It teaches you that you are not allowed to leave the Chat tab, which is the exact opposite of seamless tab switching. `stopGeneration()` (line 1818) keeps the partial answer as a message; this path calls `resetStreamingState()` and keeps nothing.
issues.fix: Track the container the task last reset for in a `@State var lastCancelledContainerId: UUID?` and wrap lines 601-615 in `if lastCancelledContainerId != activeId { ... }`, or simply move the cancel block inside the existing `if !isSameChatContainer` branch that already computes exactly this condition at line 623. Nothing else in the body needs to change.
issues.functionalityPreserved: The cross-container bleed protection the comment at line 604 describes is fully kept — it fires on a real container change, which is the only case the comment names. The `isSameChatContainer`/`isSameDocsContainer` guards at lines 623-624 already prove the author's intent was per-container, not per-appearance: history reload, suggested-question invalidation and count recalculation are all already gated that way, and only the cancellation block was left ungated. Manual stop (line 1818) and scene-phase cancellation (line 590) are untouched.

issues.what: The chat transcript force-scrolls to the bottom on every appearance. `onAppear` calls `scrollToBottom(animated: false)` with no guard, overriding the `isPinnedToBottom` state the view already maintains for exactly this purpose.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You scroll up to re-read an earlier answer, switch to Documents to check something against it, come back — and you are slammed to the newest message, with a visible 0.12s animated jump because `animated: false` still wraps the call in `withAnimation` (line 164). Finding your place again is manual work the app just undid for you.
issues.fix: Add `@State private var hasPerformedInitialScroll = false` and in `onAppear` scroll only when `!hasPerformedInitialScroll || isPinnedToBottom`, setting the flag afterwards. Keep `scrollProxy = proxy` unconditional.
issues.functionalityPreserved: The first-open jump to the newest message is kept (the flag is false on first appearance). All streaming auto-follow is untouched — the three `onChange` handlers at lines 131, 135 and 145 already gate on `isPinnedToBottom` and do the real scroll-following work. `isPinnedToBottom` is already computed from the bottom-anchor preference at line 152, so the information needed for the guard exists and is currently just ignored.

issues.what: The Atlas tab replaces its entire populated body with a loading card every time it appears. Two `.task` modifiers both call `refreshAnalysis()` on appearance (the bare one at 205 and the id-keyed one at 208), `analyze()` sets the published `isAnalyzing = true` before doing any work (LibraryVisualizationEngine.swift:359), and the body renders `analyzeLoadingCard` whenever that flag is true (line 123) even though `engine.currentProfile` still holds a valid, complete profile.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Atlas is the tab you flick to in order to glance at something. Instead of the insights and stats you left, you get a spinner card, the page collapses to a fraction of its height so your scroll position is clamped to the top, and then everything reflows back in. The data never left memory — the app just refuses to show it while it re-derives the same result.
issues.fix: Three edits, all local: delete the bare `.task` at 205 (the `.task(id:)` at 208 already runs on appearance and on id change, so coverage is identical and the duplicate analysis disappears); in `LibraryVisualizationEngine.analyze`, serve `profileCache[containerId]` into `currentProfile` synchronously when present before starting the rebuild; and change the gate at line 123 to `if engine.isAnalyzing, engine.currentProfile == nil`.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Every refresh still happens on the same triggers — appearance, container change, and pull-to-refresh (line 210) — because the id-keyed task fires on both of the first two. Nothing is cached longer than it is now: `profileCache` is already populated on every successful analysis at LibraryVisualizationEngine.swift:381 and already invalidated per container at line 341 and wholesale at 331 (ContentView.swift:395 calls the per-container invalidation on library removal), so reading it is completing a mechanism that is already fully wired and currently dead. The loading card still shows on genuine first load, when `currentProfile` is nil.

issues.what: The compact 3D atlas scene discards its rendered point cloud on every appearance. Two `.task(id:)` modifiers both fire on appear (2897, 2900), each calls `loadAndProject()`, and its first statement sets `isLoading = true` (line 3029), which swaps the SceneKit view for a spinner while up to 50,000 points are re-fetched from FTS5 and re-projected — twice, concurrently.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: The 3D atlas is the one thing in the app you orient yourself in — you rotate it to a view you like. Coming back to the tab throws away both the render and your camera position, and you watch it rebuild from a spinner. The `points`, `colors` and `annotations` arrays are still sitting in `@State` the whole time.
issues.fix: Collapse the two modifiers into one `.task(id: AtlasReloadKey(container: containerService.activeContainerId, projection: projectionMethod))` over a small `Equatable` struct, and in `loadAndProject()` set `isLoading = true` only when `points.isEmpty`, assigning the new arrays when the projection finishes.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Both reload triggers are kept verbatim: a composite Equatable key changes when either the container or the projection method changes, which is precisely the union of what the two separate ids covered. The empty-library path at line 3046 still clears the arrays and drops the spinner. The five `onChange` handlers at 2903-2907 that reload the scene for point scale, rotation, depth cue, labels and background are untouched.

issues.what: The Database tab shows "Loading database statistics..." on every return. `.task { await loadAllData() }` restarts on appearance and `loadAllData` sets `isLoading = true` at line 215 before querying, while the overview section gates its whole body on that flag at line 492 — even though `stats` and `documentStats` are still populated from the previous visit.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Database is a reference tab you bounce in and out of while working. Every bounce costs a spinner and a scroll reset on the default section, for numbers that were on screen ten seconds ago and are still in memory. The 10-second watchdog at line 218 tells you the author already knows this load can be slow — which is exactly why the previous result should stay visible during it.
issues.fix: Set `isLoading = true` at line 215 only when `stats == nil`, and change the gate at line 492 to `if isLoading, stats == nil`. Optionally add a small inline refreshing indicator in `headerSection` so the refresh is still legible.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Every phase still runs on every appearance — Phase 1 metadata, Phase 2 diagnostics and vocabulary in the detached task, Phase 3 content-table backfill. The watchdog at line 218 keeps working because it reads the same flag. `.refreshable` (line 196) and the scope-change reload (line 187) are untouched. No query is skipped or cached; only the decision to blank the screen while they run changes.

issues.what: The ingestion queue overlay exists as two independent instances — one in Chat (ChatScreen.swift:520) and one in Documents (DocumentLibraryView.swift:1327) — each holding its own `@State isMinimized` and `@State isDismissed`. Dismissing or minimizing it on one tab has no effect on the other.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You dismiss the ingestion panel to get it out of the way, switch tabs, and it is back at full size — so the dismissal reads as broken rather than tab-scoped. Worse in the other direction: you minimise it on Documents to watch progress compactly, go to Chat, and it expands over the composer again. Dismissal is a statement about the panel, not about the tab you happened to be on.
issues.fix: Introduce a small `@MainActor final class IngestionOverlayPresentation: ObservableObject` holding `isMinimized`/`isDismissed`, own it as a `@StateObject` in ContentView alongside the other stores, inject it with `.environmentObject`, and have `IngestionQueueOverlay` read it instead of its two local `@State` properties.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Every control, item row, cancel/continue/discard callback and console view stays exactly as it is — only where the two booleans live changes. The auto-reset on an emptied queue (line 475) and the deep-link un-dismiss handler (line 481) keep working unchanged against the shared object, and the deep link actually improves: it currently un-dismisses both copies blindly, and would instead un-dismiss the one panel that exists.

issues.what: No tab's `NavigationStack` takes a `path` binding, so nothing can programmatically return a tab to its root. `handleOpenURL` and the Spotlight handler set `selectedTab` only; if the target tab has a pushed detail view, the user lands on that detail instead of the destination the link named.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Tap a Spotlight result for a document while the Documents tab happens to be showing a different document's details, and you arrive at the wrong document with the app insisting it navigated. Same for the `openintelligence://documents/ingestion` deep link, which posts its overlay notification (line 419) to a screen you cannot see. It also means re-tapping the already-selected tab does nothing, breaking the pop-to-root gesture every iOS user has in their hands.
issues.fix: Add `@State private var documentsPath = NavigationPath()` (and equivalents for the other tabs that push), bind them into the `NavigationStack(path:)` initialisers at 255/263/275/285/295, clear the relevant path in `handleOpenURL` (line 416) and in the Spotlight handler (line 108) before assigning `selectedTab`, and add a `selectedTab` binding wrapper whose setter clears the path when the new value equals the old.
issues.functionalityPreserved: `NavigationStack` tracks `NavigationLink(destination:)` pushes in its bound path as well as value-based links, so the existing document-row link (DocumentLibraryView.swift:204), the Settings links (SettingsView.swift:322) and the diagnostics hub links all keep working with no call-site change. This adds reachability; it removes no destination and no way of getting to one.

issues.what: The Spotlight handler assigns `containerService.activeContainerId` directly instead of calling `setActive(_:)`, so the library switch skips both the existence guard and the UserDefaults write that `setActive` performs (ContainerService.swift:46-55).
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Opening a document from Spotlight silently puts the app in a library it will forget: relaunch and you are back in the previous one, wondering where the document went. And because the existence check is skipped, a Spotlight entry for a since-deleted library sets an active id that matches nothing, so `filteredDocuments` (DocumentLibraryView.swift:89) returns empty and the tab looks like an empty library rather than a stale link.
issues.fix: Replace the assignment with `containerService.setActive(containerId)`.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Identical navigation outcome for every valid id — `setActive` assigns the same published property on line 49. It adds the `containers.contains` guard, the UserDefaults persistence and the selection haptic that every other switch site in the app already gets. The `else` fallback at line 109 already handles the no-container case, so a rejected invalid id degrades to exactly the behaviour that branch was written for.

issues.what: The library chip strip is a plain horizontal `ScrollView` with no `ScrollViewReader`, so the active chip is never scrolled into view when the active library changes from anywhere other than a tap on a visible chip.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: With more than a few libraries, a Spotlight jump (ContentView.swift:107), a workspace reload (ContentView.swift:391), or a switch made from Semantic Search leaves you looking at a document list with the selected chip parked off-screen. There is no on-screen answer to "which library am I in", so you scroll the strip hunting for the highlighted pill before you trust anything below it.
issues.fix: Wrap the `ScrollView` in a `ScrollViewReader`, tag each pill with `.id(container.id)` inside `pillList` (line 92), and add `.onAppear` plus `.onChange(of: containerService.activeContainerId)` handlers that call `proxy.scrollTo(containerService.activeContainerId, anchor: .center)` inside a short animation.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Purely additive. The pill list, disambiguated duplicate names (line 82), the count badges, the context-menu storage and delete actions with their deliberate nil-ness (lines 108-118), and the existing `withAnimation { setActive }` tap path are all unchanged. This adds an affordance where there is currently none.

issues.what: Tab selection and the composer draft are plain `@State` with no `@SceneStorage` anywhere in the app, so neither survives state restoration after the system unloads the scene.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: The draft is the sharper half. You type out a long, carefully worded question, get pulled into another app, come back after the system has reclaimed the scene, and the composer is empty — the app persists your transcript on background (ContentView.swift:329-330) but not the sentence you had not sent yet, which is the one piece of text only you could have produced. The tab reset is milder but still jarring: the app always reopens on Chat regardless of where you were working.
issues.fix: Change `selectedTab` to `@SceneStorage`, backing it with a `String` raw value since `ContentView.Tab` (line 65) has no raw type today; add a raw-value conformance or map through a small helper. Separately change `inputText` in ChatComposerV2.swift:26 to `@SceneStorage("chatDraft")`, keeping the existing clear-on-send at line 247.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Both remain ordinary mutable state with identical read and write semantics — `@SceneStorage` only adds a persistence backing. The screenshot-mode initial-tab override (ContentView.swift:60-62) still works because it writes the same property before first render. The draft's `onChange` handler at ChatComposerV2.swift:160 and the send path that clears it at line 247 are unaffected.

results.summary: Seven real findings, all read off source with line anchors. The dominant pattern is not slowness — it is that three of the five tabs throw away content they already have in order to show a spinner. Database blanks its whole overview to "Loading database statistics..." on every return to the tab even though `stats` is still in `@State`; Atlas collapses its insights, recommended views and library stats to "Analyzing your library..." on every return even though `currentProfile` is a live singleton and a `profileCache` exists that is written, invalidated, and never once read. Atlas additionally runs its most expensive operation (full embedding hydration for the container) twice per appearance because of a redundant `.task` sitting next to a `.task(id:)`. Database's first open races its own scope seeding against its own initial load, doing every query twice and re-raising the spinner after content appeared. In Chat, the suggested-prompt card has no loading state at all: because "no results yet" and "no results, ever" are the same empty array, the card prints the terminal fail-closed verdict "No grounded suggestions are ready yet" while it is still working, then contradicts itself when chips pop in — and for any library that genuinely yields nothing, that same load is re-fired on every single entry to the Chat tab, forever. The load it is waiting on is itself mostly waste: it pulls a sample of chunks (which forces the whole vector store off disk via `allChunks()` → `awaitLoad()`), and `generateQuestions` discards that sample whenever the on-disk question bank is non-empty, which is the normal case. Two smaller flow breaks: the transcript is yanked to the bottom on every return to Chat regardless of where you were reading, and the composer text field is hard-disabled for the entire generation, so you cannot draft your next question while an answer streams. Every fix below is deferral, caching, or state-machine repair. None deletes a screen, an action, a diagnostic or a piece of copy — the fail-closed suggestion message, the 10s watchdog, the send guard, the pull-to-refresh force path and the "open at the newest message" behaviour all survive intact. Not covered here (belongs to the throughput audit): the launch hang, publisher storms, main-actor blocking, list construction. One thing I looked for and did not find: no second instance of the manual-long-press-inside-a-horizontal-ScrollView pattern survives — `ContainerPicker.swift:216-219` is now `.contextMenu` with the reasoning written down, and the only other `onLongPressGesture` (`SourceChipsView.swift:126`) uses `minimumDuration: 0` purely as a press-highlight, which does not contend with a pan.

issues.what: `loadAllData()` sets `isLoading = true` unconditionally and is attached to a bare `.task`, so returning to the Database tab replaces the entire, already-populated overview with a full-screen "Loading database statistics..." spinner while it re-fetches figures that are still sitting in `@State`.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You leave the Database tab, come back three seconds later, and the screen you were just looking at is gone — replaced by a spinner. The data never left; the app just decided to hide it from you. The team already knows this load can hang, because there is a 10-second watchdog at line 220 guarding it, which means the blank period is sometimes very long.
issues.fix: Make the spinner conditional on there being nothing to show: `if isLoading && stats == nil`. Keep rendering the existing `stats` during a refresh and let the new values swap in when they land. Optionally add a small inline refresh indicator in `headerSection` so the update is still visible. For the very first open, warm `SQLiteFullTextService.getStatistics()` from the app-level `.task` in ContentView (ContentView.swift:161) so the tab's first paint has figures ready rather than a cold spinner.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Every figure, section, watchdog and refresh path is untouched. `loadAllData()` still runs, still repopulates `stats`, `documentStats`, and all Phase 2 diagnostics, and the watchdog at line 220 still force-clears `isLoading`. The only change is which view is shown during the fetch: stale-but-real numbers instead of a spinner. On a genuinely first load `stats` is nil and the spinner still appears exactly as today, so nothing is hidden behind implied data.

issues.what: First open of the Database tab runs two overlapping loads: `.task` calls `loadAllData()` while `.onAppear` seeds `databaseScope` from `.allLibraries` to `.library(activeId)`, which fires `.onChange(of: databaseScope)` into a second `loadStatistics()`. Both set `isLoading`, so whichever finishes first reveals content and the other immediately re-hides it. `loadStatistics` also calls `getIndexInfo()` in the blocking path — the query `loadAllData` deliberately pushed to Phase 2 at line 246 precisely so it could never block the UI.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: The tab flashes: spinner, content, spinner, content. And every later scope change (picking a different library from the picker at line 444) wipes all four metric cards to a spinner rather than updating the numbers in place, so comparing two libraries means watching the screen empty out between each one.
issues.fix: Two changes. (a) Seed the scope before the load can observe it — give `databaseScope` its value in the same `.onAppear` that already guards on `didSeedScope`, and make the `.onChange(of: databaseScope)` handler skip while `didSeedScope` has only just been set, or simply initialise the scope from `containerService.activeContainerId` and drop the seeding `onAppear` entirely. (b) In `loadStatistics` (line 1534), stop blanking: leave the previous `stats`/`documentStats` on screen and swap them when the new ones arrive, and move `getIndexInfo()` out of the blocking sequence into the same detached follow-up `loadAllData` uses for it.
issues.functionalityPreserved: The scope still defaults to the active library, which is the documented intent in the comment at lines 32-34. Every query still runs and every value still refreshes; `getIndexInfo()` still populates `indexInfo`, just off the critical path exactly as `loadAllData` already does at line 246. The duplicate load is removed, not the work — the surviving load fetches a strict superset. The `indexSection` at line 945 already has its own "Loading index info..." branch for when `indexInfo` is nil, so deferring it is a state the UI is already built to render honestly.

issues.what: `AdaptiveVisualizationsView` carries a bare `.task { await refreshAnalysis() }` immediately above `.task(id: containerService.activeContainerId) { await refreshAnalysis() }`. The id-based one already fires on first appearance, so the bare one is pure duplication — and `refreshAnalysis` awaits `ragService.allChunksForActiveContainer()` (RAGService.swift:3872), which hydrates an embedding for every chunk in the container, before `engine.analyze` is reached. Both copies run that hydration concurrently with no cancellation between them.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Opening Atlas costs twice what it needs to, and the duplicate work happens at exactly the moment the user is staring at a spinner waiting for the tab to resolve.
issues.fix: Delete the bare `.task` at lines 205-207. `.task(id:)` at 208-210 fires on appearance and on every container change, which is a strict superset of what the bare one covered.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Nothing. `.task(id:)` runs on initial appearance and on id change; the bare `.task` runs only on initial appearance. Removing it cannot drop a trigger. Pull-to-refresh at line 211 is a separate modifier and is untouched.

issues.what: While a re-analysis runs, `engine.isAnalyzing` swaps the insights row, recommended-views grid, any expanded view and the library stats for a large "Analyzing your library..." card — even though `engine.currentProfile` is still populated (the engine is `LibraryVisualizationEngine.shared`, so it survives tab switches). Meanwhile `hero3DAtlasSection` at line 117 reads the same live profile and keeps rendering. Worse, `LibraryVisualizationEngine` maintains a `profileCache` (LibraryVisualizationEngine.swift:304) that is written at line 381 and invalidated at 332/341 but is never read anywhere in the codebase, so `analyze()` recomputes from scratch every time.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Return to Atlas and the screen tears in half: the 3D scene is still there, fully rendered from a profile the app clearly still has, while everything beneath it has been replaced by a spinner claiming the library needs analysing. The app is visibly withholding data it is simultaneously displaying six inches higher up. The same repo does this correctly elsewhere — `ProjectionCache` (Embedding3DView.swift:3202-3231) checks its cache before recomputing — so the write-only `profileCache` reads as an oversight rather than a decision.
issues.fix: Two parts. (a) In the view, change the branch to `if engine.isAnalyzing && engine.currentProfile == nil` so a refresh keeps the last profile on screen; move the analysing signal to a small inline indicator near `libraryHeader`. (b) In `LibraryVisualizationEngine.analyze`, actually read `profileCache`: add a cheap fingerprint (containerId plus documents.count, chunks.count, retrievalHistory.count) to the cached entry and return early — publishing the cached profile, insights and recommended views without setting `isAnalyzing` — when the fingerprint matches. Add a `force: Bool = false` parameter so `.refreshable` (line 211) can bypass the cache.
issues.functionalityPreserved: The analysing card still shows on a true cold analysis, when `currentProfile` is nil. Every insight, recommended view, expanded view and stat is computed by the same code path and is byte-identical; the cache only skips recomputing a result that the existing invalidation hooks (`invalidateCache(for:)`, already wired from ContentView.swift:395) already guarantee is stale-free. Pull-to-refresh keeps its exact current force-recompute behaviour via the new `force` flag. No placeholder is invented — the view shows a real previously-computed profile, not a guess.

issues.what: The starter-prompt card has no loading state. `refreshSuggestedQuestions` only sets `isRefreshingSuggestions = true` inside `if force` (line 1648), so the non-forced path used on library switch and on tab entry never signals that it is working. With `dynamicSuggestedQuestions` cleared to `[]` at line 643, `starterPrompts` returns `[]` (line 1587), and `FirstQueryPromptView.supportingText` therefore prints its terminal fail-closed verdict — "No grounded suggestions are ready yet" (line 3744) — while the load is still in flight. Because an in-progress load and a genuinely empty result are the same empty array, `onAppear` (line 883) and `.task(id:)` (line 654) both re-fire the whole load on every single entry to the Chat tab for any library that legitimately yields no questions.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You tap a library chip and the app immediately tells you there is nothing to suggest — a settled, confident-sounding verdict — and then a second later contradicts itself by filling the card with chips. That is the opposite of the honesty this UI is built for: it states a conclusion it has not reached. And on a library that really does yield nothing, the app silently redoes the entire lookup every time you touch the Chat tab and prints the identical sentence.
issues.fix: Introduce a tri-state (`notLoaded` / `loading` / `loaded(questions)`) for the suggestions, replacing the `dynamicSuggestedQuestions.isEmpty` proxy. Set `loading` at the top of `refreshSuggestedQuestions` regardless of `force` (or add a separate `isLoadingSuggestions` flag alongside the existing `isRefreshingSuggestions`, which drives the spin animation on the refresh button). Give `supportingText` a loading branch that describes the action rather than promising an outcome — "Looking for grounded suggestions in this library…" — and show 3-4 dimmed skeleton rows in place of the prompt list. Keep the existing sentence at line 3744 for the `loaded` state with zero results. Gate the re-fire at lines 654 and 883 on the state being `notLoaded`, not on the array being empty.
issues.functionalityPreserved: The fail-closed message at line 3744 is kept verbatim and still shows whenever the load actually resolves with no grounded questions — that behaviour is the point of the design (see the header comment in SuggestedQuestionsService.swift:32) and is untouched. The manual refresh button, its spin animation, and the `force: true` path all keep working identically. The skeleton rows carry no text and imply no specific content, so they cannot suggest data that may not arrive; the loading sentence describes what the app is doing, not what it will find. Gating the retry on `notLoaded` does not remove a refresh route: document changes still invalidate through `.onReceive(ragService.$documents)` at line 661 and the user can still force a regeneration from the refresh button.

issues.what: Before the suggestion chips can appear, `refreshSuggestedQuestions` awaits `ragService.getSampleChunks(for:limit:)` for up to 160 chunks. That call goes to `db.allChunks()` (RAGService.swift:3928), which in `BNNSVectorDatabase` begins with `await awaitLoad()` (BNNSVectorDatabase.swift:680) — pulling the container's entire vector store off disk. `generateQuestions` then uses `sampleChunks` only when the on-disk question bank is empty (SuggestedQuestionsService.swift:488), and the bank is normally non-empty, so the whole fetch is discarded. The eager `await suggestedQuestionsService.invalidateCache(for: activeId)` at line 650 — invalidating the cache for the library being switched *to* — guarantees `hasValidCache` returns false and the fetch is always paid.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Tapping a library chip should be instant — `ContainerService.setActive` is just a UUID assignment and a UserDefaults write. Instead the chip highlights, the prompt card goes blank, and you wait on a full vector-store load for a value that is then thrown away. The cost scales with library size, so the bigger your library the worse switching into it feels, for no reason connected to what is being displayed.
issues.fix: Stop materialising the sample eagerly. Change `generateQuestions` to take a lazy provider — `sampleChunks: @Sendable () async throws -> [DocumentChunk]` — and invoke it only inside the `if bank.isEmpty` branch at SuggestedQuestionsService.swift:488. The caller then passes `{ try await ragService.getSampleChunks(for: containerId, limit: sampleLimit) }` and pays nothing on the common path. Separately, drop the eager `invalidateCache(for: activeId)` at line 650: it targets the library being switched to, so it only destroys the fast path. The cache is already invalidated on real content change via `.onReceive(ragService.$documents)` at line 670 and by `removeQuestions`/`clearQuestionBank` in the service.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Identical questions are produced. When the bank is empty the provider is called and `generateInitialBank` runs exactly as today, with the same limit computed the same way at line 1685. When the bank is non-empty the fetched value was already being discarded, so skipping it cannot change any output. Removing the eager invalidation does not stale the chips: the document-change hook at line 670 and the `documentCount` check inside `hasValidCache` (SuggestedQuestionsService.swift:591) both still force regeneration when the library's contents actually change, and the manual refresh button still forces unconditionally.

issues.what: `MessageListV2` calls `scrollToBottom(proxy:animated:false)` from an unconditional `.onAppear`, ignoring the `isPinnedToBottom` state it maintains at line 173 for exactly this purpose.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You scroll up to re-read an earlier answer, hop to Documents to check a source, come back — and you are dumped at the bottom of the transcript with no way back to where you were except scrolling again. The app forgets what you were reading every time you glance at another tab.
issues.fix: Gate the call: `if isPinnedToBottom { scrollToBottom(proxy: proxy, animated: false) }`. `isPinnedToBottom` is `@State`, initialised `true`, and is maintained by the preference-key handler at line 150, so a first appearance and any return-while-already-at-the-bottom still land at the newest message. If a device check shows SwiftUI is not preserving the scroll offset across tab switches on its own, keep a `@State lastVisibleMessageID` fed by the same preference machinery and `proxy.scrollTo` that id instead — restoring the position rather than abandoning it.
issues.functionalityPreserved: "Open the chat at the newest message" is kept: `isPinnedToBottom` starts `true`, so the first appearance behaves exactly as today, as does every return where the user had not scrolled away. Auto-follow during streaming (lines 132-149) is a different code path and is untouched; it already correctly guards on `isPinnedToBottom`. Nothing is removed — the only behaviour that changes is the one case that currently discards user state.

issues.what: The composer's `TextField` is `.disabled(isProcessing)`, so for the entire duration of a generation — which in Deep Think and Maximum modes is many seconds — the user cannot type, and the keyboard is dismissed because a disabled field resigns first responder. The attachment button also vanishes entirely at line 93.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: The moment you send a question the app takes the keyboard away from you. Any follow-up you had half-formed has to wait, and when the answer finishes you have to tap back into the field and start typing from scratch. Every other chat interface lets you draft while the reply streams.
issues.fix: Remove `.disabled(isProcessing)` from the TextField and add `guard canSend else { return }` at the top of `send()` (line 218), which reinstates the exact block the `.disabled` was providing — `canSend` already requires `!isProcessing` at line 47. Keep the attachment button mounted but disabled rather than removing it at line 93, so the composer does not resize mid-generation. The send button already becomes Stop during processing (lines 128-148) and needs no change.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Sending during generation stays blocked, and now by an explicit guard rather than a side effect of a view modifier — which also closes a real gap, since `ChatScreen.sendMessage` (ChatScreen.swift:2471) has no `isProcessing` check of its own while `sendMessageWithAttachments` does (line 2318), so the `.disabled` was the only thing stopping the `onSubmit(send)` path at line 157. Stop, attachment picking, and every other composer affordance are unchanged; the attachment button becomes disabled rather than absent, so nothing is lost and the layout stops jumping.

results.summary:
Nine real deferral opportunities, all verified against source. The launch shape is the main story: `ContentView.init` (ContentView.swift:27-63) synchronously builds eight services on the main thread before the first frame, and the heaviest thing in that chain is a CoreML model load nothing on the first frame needs. `WindowGroup { ContentView() }` means every one of those initialisers runs before SwiftUI has anything to draw.

For tab first-appearance, the pattern that recurs is not "slow work" but "the same work twice". Atlas has both a bare `.task` and a `.task(id:)` on the same view, so its full chunk load and analysis run twice on first open. Database seeds its scope in `.onAppear`, which trips an `.onChange` that runs a second load concurrently with the `.task` load, and the two fight over one `isLoading` flag. Neither costs a capability to fix; one is a line deletion.

Two findings are about work that is already cached or already static being recomputed: `LibraryVisualizationEngine.profileCache` is written on every analysis and read nowhere, so returning to a library you already looked at re-derives everything from scratch while the screen collapses to a spinner. And `EmbeddingService.forProvider` loads the full MiniLM model just to answer two constants, which is what makes both "Create Library" and opening Container Settings hitch.

I deliberately did not report `ContentView.onChange(of:)` string-building, publisher fan-out, or list construction. That is the throughput audit's ground. Where I do touch I/O (finding 7) the claim is about *when* it runs, not how fast it is.

One correction worth stating: I initially read the hardware-telemetry singleton as booting a feature that is off. It is not. `showSiliconHUD` defaults to `true` (SettingsStore.swift:581). Finding 8 is written to the narrower, true version.

Everything about actual magnitude needs a device. SwiftUI's TabView appear/disappear semantics in particular decide whether finding 4 is a once-per-session annoyance or a once-per-tab-switch one, and I cannot settle that from source.

issues.what: The CoreML sentence-embedding model is loaded synchronously on the main thread inside ContentView.init, before the first frame. ContentView.swift:41 builds RAGService, whose init at RAGService.swift:1542 constructs `EmbeddingService()`, whose default parameter (EmbeddingService.swift:53) constructs `CoreMLSentenceEmbeddingProvider()`. That initialiser (CoreMLSentenceEmbeddingProvider.swift:83-94) touches `DeviceCapabilityService.shared` at :91 (which probes chip, memory and creates a Metal snapshot, DeviceCapabilityService.swift:224-235), pre-allocates the MLMultiArray pool at :92, then calls setup() at :93, which runs `try MLModel(contentsOf: url, configuration: config)` at :168. Nothing drawn in the first frame needs an embedder; the first real consumer is a query or an ingest.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: The gap between tapping the icon and seeing anything is spent on a model the user has not asked to use yet. The app is doing machine-learning setup while the launch screen sits there, so the very first impression of the app is a wait for work that will not be needed for several more seconds at the earliest.
issues.fix: Keep the eager construction of EmbeddingService but make the provider's model load asynchronous behind an awaitable readiness handle: move the `MLModel(contentsOf:)` call out of `setup()` into a `Task(priority: .utility)` started from init, exactly as the tokenizer load at :190-197 already does, and have `embed(text:)` await that handle before its first use. Kick it from ContentView's existing `.task` (ContentView.swift:161) if you want it deterministically after first frame rather than racing it.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Same provider, same compute units, same 384 dimensions, same fallback chain in `EmbeddingService.forProvider`. The model is still loaded, still with `DeviceCapabilityService.shared.preferredComputeUnits`, and `enableIngestionMode()`/`disableIngestionMode()` still swap it the same way. The one thing that must not be done naively: `isAvailable` currently answers `model != nil` (CoreMLSentenceEmbeddingProvider.swift:203-215), so a lazy load would make it report false during the window. The readiness handle must be awaited by `isAvailable`'s callers rather than letting them see a transient false, or the fallback chain in forProvider will pick the wrong provider. That is the whole risk in this change.

issues.what: AdaptiveVisualizationsView attaches two `.task` modifiers that call the same function. `.task { await refreshAnalysis() }` at line 205-207 and `.task(id: containerService.activeContainerId) { await refreshAnalysis() }` at line 208-210 both fire on first appearance. `refreshAnalysis` (:818-835) calls `ragService.allChunksForActiveContainer()`, which loads every chunk in the container and, for mmap-backed stores, hydrates every embedding (RAGService.swift:3872-3900). `engine.analyze` cancels the previous analysisTask (LibraryVisualizationEngine.swift:356), so the second run's analysis is thrown away, but only after the expensive chunk load has already happened twice.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: The first time you tap Atlas it takes about twice as long as it should to show anything, and the wait scales with library size, so the tab feels progressively heavier the more you put in the app. The tab that is supposed to show off the library is the slowest one to open.
issues.fix: Delete the bare `.task` at lines 205-207. `.task(id:)` already runs on initial appearance as well as on every change of `activeContainerId`, so it covers both cases the pair was written for.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Exactly. `.task(id:)` fires on first appearance and on every subsequent id change; the bare `.task` fires only on first appearance. The bare one is a strict subset. Refresh-on-container-switch and refresh-on-open both continue to work, and `.refreshable` at :211-213 is untouched.

issues.what: DatabaseDashboardView runs two overlapping loads on its first appearance and they contend for one loading flag. `.task` at :180-183 runs `loadAllData()`. Separately, `.onAppear` at :191-195 seeds `databaseScope` from its `.allLibraries` default (:35) to `.library(activeContainerId)`, which is always a change on first appearance, which fires `.onChange(of: databaseScope)` at :188-190, which runs `loadStatistics()`. Both hit the same `SQLiteFullTextService.shared` actor so the queries serialise, and both write `isLoading` (loadAllData at :215 and :241, loadStatistics at :1535 and :1540).
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Opening the Database tab takes noticeably longer than the work justifies, and the spinner can come back after content has already appeared, which reads as the screen changing its mind. A screen that flickers between loaded and loading feels broken even when the numbers it eventually shows are correct.
issues.fix: Seed the scope somewhere that cannot trigger a reload. Either set `didSeedScope = true` and assign `databaseScope` before the onChange can observe it, or have the `.onChange` handler return early for the seeding transition (guard on `didSeedScope` having just flipped). Then `.task` is the single loader on first open and `.onChange` only serves genuine user scope changes.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Same data, same default scope (the active library, which is what the comment at :32-34 says it wants), same reload when the user actually picks a different scope from the picker, same `.refreshable` path at :199-201. Only the redundant first-open load disappears. Phase 2 diagnostics loading at :246-260 is unaffected.

issues.what: LibraryVisualizationEngine keeps a `profileCache` (declared at :304, written at :381) that is never read. `invalidateCache(for:)` at :340-345 only removes from it. So `analyze` (:350-386) unconditionally rebuilds the profile even when the exact profile for that container is already in the dictionary. Compounding it, AdaptiveVisualizationsView.swift:123-125 branches `if engine.isAnalyzing { analyzeLoadingCard } else if let profile = engine.currentProfile`, so insights, recommended views, the expanded view and the stats section all vanish for the duration of any re-analysis, while the hero atlas at :117 keeps rendering the stale profile because it reads `currentProfile` outside that branch.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Switching library away and back, or pulling to refresh, throws the whole screen away and puts you back at a spinner, even though you were just looking at the answer. Half the screen keeps its old content and half of it empties, which looks like a glitch rather than a load. Going back to somewhere you have already been should be the fastest thing the app does, and here it is one of the slowest.
issues.fix: Two changes. In `analyze`, before starting the rebuild, publish `profileCache[containerId]` into `currentProfile`/`insights`/`recommendedViews` if it exists, so the previous answer is on screen instantly. In the view, invert the branch to `if let profile = engine.currentProfile { ...content... }` and render the analysing state as an inline indicator next to `libraryHeader`, falling back to `analyzeLoadingCard` only when there is genuinely no profile yet.
issues.functionalityPreserved: The analysis still runs in full and still replaces the profile when it completes; nothing is skipped or approximated, and `invalidateCache(for:)` still forces a genuine rebuild after a container is deleted (ContentView.swift:395). The user sees the previous result instead of a spinner, which is strictly more information than a spinner, not less. The `isAnalyzing` state remains observable and remains shown, just not as a replacement for the content.

issues.what: Opening the Container Settings sheet loads the CoreML model once per embedding-provider option, on the main actor. `.onAppear` at :283 calls `refreshProviderAvailability()` (:579-605), which loops `embeddingProviderOptions` and calls `EmbeddingService.forProvider(id:targetDimension:allowFallback: false)` for each just to read `service.isAvailable`. Each of those constructs a fresh provider, and the CoreML branches in EmbeddingService.swift (:133, :141, :148, :171) each run `MLModel(contentsOf:)` synchronously. The `Task { }` at :580 is not detached, and `View` is `@MainActor`, so it inherits main-actor isolation and the loop body runs on the main actor.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: The sheet stalls partway through its presentation animation, so the slide-up stutters or lands late. It also happens again every time the active container changes (:290-293), so the screen keeps freezing on interactions that should be instant.
issues.fix: Make the probe loop `Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated)` so it cannot occupy the main actor during the sheet transition, and memoise the per-provider availability result so the repeat call at :293 does not redo the loads. Better still, answer availability from a lightweight probe rather than a full `EmbeddingService` construction, since availability only needs to know whether the model file resolves and loads.
issues.functionalityPreserved: The same `providerAvailability` dictionary is computed from the same `forProvider` resolution with the same `allowFallback: false`, so every provider still reports the same availability and the unavailable-provider warning at :600-602 still fires. The CoreAI `awaitReady()` call at :582-584 stays where it is. Nothing about which providers the user can pick changes.

issues.what: Creating a library builds a full EmbeddingService, and therefore loads the CoreML model, purely to read two static values. `createNewLibrary` is `@MainActor` (:1509) and calls `EmbeddingService.forProvider(id:allowFallback:)` at :1522, then uses the result only for `.actualProviderId` and `.outputDimension` at :1531-1532. The native dimension for every provider id is already a compile-time constant in the `nativeDimensions` table at EmbeddingService.swift:75-81.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You tap Create and the app goes dead for a moment before the library appears. It is the most direct kind of unresponsiveness: a button press that does not visibly do anything for long enough to make you wonder whether it registered.
issues.fix: Memoise the provider resolution. Resolve (provider id, dimension) once per provider id, off the critical path, and have `createNewLibrary` read the memoised pair. The resolution function is the same `forProvider` logic; it just does not need to run its model load again on a UI action to return an answer it has already computed.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Same provider id and same dimension written into the new container, and the same fallback outcome, because the memoised value comes from the same resolution function rather than from a reimplementation of it. Do not cache the `EmbeddingService` instance itself for reuse here: RAGService.swift:5363 calls `enableIngestionMode()` on a per-container service, and sharing one instance would leak ingestion-mode compute-unit changes across unrelated callers. Cache the resolved metadata, not the service.

issues.what: RAGService.init reads and decodes the document metadata file synchronously on the main thread. `loadDocumentsFromDisk()` is called at RAGService.swift:1654, inside an init that runs from ContentView.swift:41, which runs inside `ContentView.init` before the first frame. The `Task { @MainActor }` at :3641 defers only the *application* of the result; the actual `WorkspaceSyncService.coordinatedReadData` plus `JSONDecoder().decode([Document].self, from: data)` at :3653-3654 happen inline on the calling thread.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Launch is longer than it needs to be, and it gets longer the more documents you have, so the app feels like it is punishing you for using it. Nothing on the first frame depends on this list.
issues.fix: Move the read itself inside the existing Task, not just the apply: make `loadDocumentsFromDisk()` start a `Task` that calls `loadDocumentsSnapshotFromDisk()` and then hops to `@MainActor` for `applyLoadedDocuments`. The apply step is already async and already handles arriving after the view exists.
issues.functionalityPreserved: The same file is read with the same coordinated read, decoded the same way, and applied through the same `applyLoadedDocuments` path, which already runs asynchronously today and already recomputes `totalChunksStored`, calls `syncAllContainerStats()` and kicks `refreshIntelligence`. Consumers already tolerate arriving-later documents: ChatScreen recomputes its counts from `.task(id:)` (ChatScreen.swift:600) and from `.onReceive(ragService.$documents)` (:661). This overlaps the throughput audit's territory on the read cost; the claim here is only about when it runs.

issues.what: The hardware telemetry sampling loops start at singleton construction and never stop, regardless of whether anything is displaying them. `HardwareTelemetryState.init` (:333-336) starts `startHistoryRecording()`, a perpetual @MainActor task waking every 200 ms to append and trim four arrays (:739-746, :748-764), and `startRealCPUMonitoring()`, which subscribes to `SystemStateMonitor.shared` delivered on the main queue (:350-355) and starts a second perpetual task polling Mach CPU counters every 500 ms (:358-366). `SystemStateMonitor.init` in turn enables battery monitoring and starts its own repeating Timer (SystemStateMonitor.swift:287-301, :629-635).
